native_result.query: In which century did the Diversity in Pottery Form collapses and Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases simultaneuosly?
native_result.HypoA: Around 1800 BCE, Diversity in Pottery Form collapses, while Diversity in Pottery Decoration increases.
native_result.HypoB: Pottery Form diversity collapses and Pottery Decoration diversity increases simultaneously in the 17th century BCE (1700 BCE). The collapsed PotteryForm Z-value (−1.13) and elevated PotteryDecoration Z-value (0.97) are first observed together at the 1700 BCE data point (17th c. BCE, 1700–1601 BCE); the change is registered on the 1800→1700 BCE step, where PotteryForm drops 0.74→−1.13 (Δ=−1.87, z=−3.33, the largest collapse in the series) while PotteryDecoration rises −0.48→0.97 (Δ=+1.45, z=+3.14, the largest increase in the series).
native_result.WorkflowB: Used raw PotteryForm and PotteryDecoration Z-values from time_series_data.csv (37 samples at 100-year spacing, CE −4100..−500; CE is the time label, BCE negative). Computed first differences and their z-scores on the 100-year series and selected the step with the strongest simultaneous Form-collapse (dForm<<0) and Decoration-increase (dDeco>>0). Cross-checked with the annual interpolated columns (PotteryForm_inter/PotteryDecoration_inter), which confirm a monotonic transition confined to the −1800..−1700 window. Pollen/openness data was not used for this sub-question.

These opposite changes occur simultaneously; annual interpolated columns confirm a monotonic transition confined to CE −1800..−1700.
